_request.system:
You classify a single ERP requirement into exactly one of four delivery tiers, using only the SAP standard-process knowledge entries provided to you.

  Fit           The delivered standard already does this once baseline org structures exist.
  Configuration The delivered logic does this, driven by values maintained in customizing                 (thresholds, code lists, org units, number ranges, determination rules). No code.
  Enhancement   The standard process still drives the flow, but a delivered object must carry an                 extra custom field, or extra logic must run at a published extension point.
  Development   The standard provides no object, no process, and no extension point covering the                 request; a new program, interface, or persistence must be built and maintained.

Method:
- Reason from the knowledge entries' stated boundaries: what the standard covers, what is a   configuration point, and what is stated to be beyond the standard.
- Do NOT classify from surface features. "It mentions an external system" is not a reason.   The reason must be that the standard provides no object, process, or extension point for it,   and that the transport, mapping, scheduling, and error handling are project deliverables.
- A requirement to make an already-delivered field required is field-status configuration.   A requirement to enforce entry in a field the delivered object does not have, or to gate a   process on a condition the standard data model does not carry, is an enhancement.
- In rationale, cite the specific entry IDs whose boundary decided the call, and say what that   boundary is. Cite only entries you were given.
- Set confidence below 0.7 when the entries conflict or none of them squarely covers the request.
_request.user:
Requirement (P2P): Rush orders for safety-critical spare parts must include a mandatory justification field before the purchase order is released.

Verbatim from the workshop: "rush orders for safety-critical spare parts need a mandatory justification field before the PO is released"

Knowledge entries retrieved for this requirement:

### KB-XC-004 — Mandatory fields and conditional validations: where the boundary sits [cross_cutting]
Standard process: Requiring an entry in a field is not automatically a configuration task, and not automatically an extension. The distinguishing question is whether the field exists on the delivered object and whether the condition that triggers the requirement is expressible in delivered controls. Making an existing, delivered field required for a given document type or transaction is field status configuration. Requiring an entry in a field that the standard object does not have, or refusing to release a document unless a check passes whose trigger depends on a business attribute the standard does not model, needs logic placed at an extension point together with a custom field to hold the value. The process is still the standard process; it is being extended, not replaced.
Capabilities covered by the standard: Field status groups control whether delivered fields are required, optional, displayed, or suppressed.; Delivered validation and substitution frameworks evaluate rules against delivered fields.; Extension points are exposed at save and release of major documents.
Common configuration points: Field status per document type, transaction, or account group.; Rule-based validations built on delivered fields.
Typically beyond the standard: Adding a custom field to a delivered document and making it mandatory under a business condition.; Blocking a delivered process step based on a classification the standard data model does not carry.; Validations that must read a value maintained outside the ERP system.

### KB-O2C-004 — Delivery blocks, export control, and trade compliance [O2C]
Standard process: A sales order or a delivery can be blocked, and the delivered blocking reasons are customizing entries assigned per document type and per customer. Trade compliance is delivered as dedicated content that screens business partners against denied party lists, classifies products against export control regulations, and checks whether a licence exists before a delivery may be released. Where a project instead requires that a human review has taken place and that its reference number is recorded on the document before release, the delivered compliance check has nothing to read: the reference field does not exist on the delivered document, so the field must be added and the release must be gated from an extension point.
Capabilities covered by the standard: Delivery and billing blocks with configurable reasons.; Denied party screening and product classification against export regulations.; Licence determination and licence-based release of deliveries.; Blocking documents until compliance checks pass.
Common configuration points: Delivery block reasons and their effect on subsequent documents.; Which document types and delivery types are subject to compliance checks.; Legal regulations, licence types, and screening parameters.
Typically beyond the standard: Requiring a bespoke review reference on the order before delivery release is permitted.; Compliance decisions recorded in an application outside the ERP system and read at release time.

### KB-P2P-003 — Extending purchasing documents with custom fields and checks [P2P]
Standard process: The purchasing document carries a defined set of header and item fields. When a project needs to capture information the delivered document does not hold, the document can be extended with custom fields that are added to the persistence, the user interface, and where relevant the released APIs. Logic that must run when the document is saved, checked, or released is placed at published extension points rather than by modifying delivered code. A requirement that says a buyer must enter a reason, a justification, or a reference before a document may proceed, where the field to hold that text does not exist on the delivered document, is an extension of the standard process rather than a change to it: the release framework itself continues to work exactly as delivered.
Capabilities covered by the standard: Custom fields can be added to purchasing document header and item and surfaced on the user interface.; Extension points run at save, at check, and at release of purchasing documents.; Custom fields can be exposed on released APIs and in analytical views.
Common configuration points: Field status control over delivered purchasing fields.; Screen layout per document type and per transaction.
Typically beyond the standard: A mandatory custom text or reference field enforced before release, keyed to a business classification.; Conditional checks that depend on a material or supplier attribute the standard document does not carry.; Cross-document checks reaching into data the delivered check cannot reach.

### KB-MD-006 — Hazardous materials and dangerous goods handling [master_data]
Standard process: The delivered product master carries indicators that flag a product as relevant for hazardous substances, and dedicated environment, health, and safety content maintains substance data, dangerous goods classifications, and the checks that stop a delivery when the classification is missing or not released. Where a project invents its own classification scheme that does not correspond to the delivered dangerous goods regulations and their released statuses, the delivered check cannot read it: the scheme has to be held in a custom field or classification and the block has to be raised from an extension point in the delivery process.
Capabilities covered by the standard: Hazardous substance relevance indicator on the product master.; Dangerous goods master with regulation-specific classifications and release status.; Delivery and shipment checks against dangerous goods classification.; Documents and phrases generated from substance data.
Common configuration points: Dangerous goods regulations and their check profiles.; Which document types and delivery types trigger a dangerous goods check.; Classification class types and characteristics.
Typically beyond the standard: A project-defined internal handling class that the delivered dangerous goods check does not recognize.; Blocking shipment until a bespoke internal review has been recorded.

parsed.rationale: The requirement is for a mandatory justification field on rush orders for safety-critical spare parts before PO release. The standard purchasing document does not include a justification field (KB-P2P-003 states 'the field to hold that text does not exist on the delivered document'). Adding such a field and enforcing it at release requires a custom field and logic placed at extension points, which is an enhancement (KB-P2P-003: 'is an extension of the standard process'). KB-XC-004 confirms that requiring a field the standard object does not have and gating release on a condition the standard data model does not carry is an extension. The standard release framework remains unchanged.
